module purpose: neorv32_spi is a bus-controlled SPI controller. It stores control settings, queues 9-bit transmit entries, generates SPI clock/data/chip-select outputs, samples incoming SPI data into a receive path, reports status and received bytes through the bus response, and can raise an interrupt.

use-case flows.value: SPI operating-mode settings (enable, phase, polarity, prescaler, divider, highspeed) written into held control state and then used to clear FIFOs, enable the engine, and pace or shape the serial clock
interrupt-condition enable settings written into held control state and used to qualify irq_o
a queued 9-bit transmit entry (command tag plus payload byte) written to the transmit FIFO and then consumed to start either chip-select update or byte transfer
SPI transfer sequencing, including clock-step generation, serial-data shifting, input sampling, transfer completion, and chip-select driving
interrupt request reflecting selected receive, transmit-empty, transmit-not-half-full, or idle conditions
control/status bits and the next received byte returned on bus reads
control registers, IRQ output, transfer engine state, chip-select output, and clock-divider state forced to defaults while rstn_i='0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores ctrl.enable, ctrl.cpha, ctrl.cpol, ctrl.prsc, ctrl.cdiv, and ctrl.highspeed on control-register writes at lines 140-145. Those stored values directly control FIFO clearing (lines 211, 243), engine enable (line 281), serial-clock levels and phase behavior (lines 286, 300-301, 309, 320, 324, 331), divider operation (lines 369-377), and the exported clock-generator enable at line 383, so corruption makes the implemented SPI mode and pacing incorrect; availability is also established because the settings are retained in edge-triggered registers and returned on reads at lines 153-158.

The configure flow stores ctrl.irq_rx_avail, ctrl.irq_tx_empty, ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf, and ctrl.irq_idle on control writes at lines 146-149. The IRQ generator then derives irq_o from these stored enables together with rx/tx/busy conditions at lines 255-259, so corruption changes which implemented conditions can raise an interrupt; availability is also established because the bits persist in registers and are reported on reads at lines 164-167.

The operate flow depends on the engine state machine and counters: rtx_engine.state is the case selector at line 282 and transitions at lines 293, 303, 312, 322, 325, and 333; rtx_engine.bitcnt is reset at line 287 and incremented at line 311; rtx_engine.done is asserted at line 321 and copied to rx_fifo.we at line 245; rtx_engine.busy is computed from state at line 340 and used in idle IRQ qualification at line 259 and busy status at line 172. Corrupting this sequencing state breaks the implemented transfer phases, completion point, and busy/idle decision; availability is also established because, when enabled and clock steps occur, the state advances and returns to idle by these rules.

A queued command entry is packed into tx_fifo.wdata at line 213, and when the consumed FIFO word has its tag bit set, the engine stores tx_fifo.rdata(3 downto 0) into rtx_engine.cs_ctrl at lines 289-290. The chip_select process then drives all chip-selects high except the indexed bit driven low when rtx_engine.cs_ctrl(3)='1' at lines 352-354, so corruption selects the wrong external target; availability is established because the selected output remains asserted by the registered cs_ctrl state until changed or cleared.

The module computes and stores the serial-clock level in rtx_engine.sck: it is forced to ctrl.cpol in idle or completion paths at lines 286, 320, and 331, and driven from ctrl.cpha/ctrl.cpol combinations during active phases at lines 301, 309, and 324. Line 344 copies that registered value to spi_clk_o, so the external SPI consumer depends on receiving exactly this implemented waveform; availability is established when the enabled divider logic raises spi_clk_en at line 373 and the transceiver updates sck on its active states.

The start flow packs a queued transmit entry into tx_fifo.wdata at line 213. In the operate flow, when a consumed FIFO word is available and its tag bit is not set, rtx_engine.sreg loads tx_fifo.rdata(7 downto 0) and the engine enters transfer at lines 288-293; spi_dat_o is then derived from the shift register MSB at line 343 while line 318 shifts the remaining bits. Corruption changes the byte serialized onto the SPI data output; availability is established because, once loaded, the state machine and clock steps continue the shift sequence through lines 303, 312, 318, 321, and 325.

The receive path samples spi_dat_i into rtx_engine.sdi_sync at line 310, shifts the sampled bit into rtx_engine.sreg at line 318, and presents the assembled byte to rx_fifo.wdata at line 244; line 245 writes that value into the receive FIFO when rtx_engine.done is asserted, and line 174 later returns the buffered byte on a data-register read. Integrity is established because the stored receive byte must equal the sampled serial-input sequence defined by lines 310 and 318; availability is established because completed transfers generate done at line 321 and feed the receive buffer.

The report flow computes irq_o on each rising edge from ctrl.enable and the selected receive, transmit-empty, transmit-not-half-full, or idle conditions at lines 255-259, with reset forcing '0' at line 253. By the module-level boundary assumption, the interrupt consumer must receive exactly the event defined by that expression, so integrity is established; availability is established under clk_i whenever the configured condition expression is true.
